subject: Life Skills
title: Handling Failure Constructively
description: A micro-lesson that makes Handling Failure Constructively usable.

hook.text: J.K. Rowling was rejected by 12 publishers. She framed the letters as proof she tried, not proof she failed.

buildup.text: Failure triggers shame because we tie outcomes to identity. 'I failed' becomes 'I am a failure.'

discovery.text: Growth mindset separates performance from identity. Failure is data about what to adjust, not who you are.

twist.text: Avoiding failure guarantees mediocrity. Every meaningful achievement requires risks that sometimes don't pay off.

climax.text: After a failure, ask three questions: what worked, what didn't, and what will I do differently next time?

punchline.text: Failure is feedback. Adjust and move forward.

quiz.question: What is the key principle of a growth mindset after failure?
options: Ignore the failure and try something different
Treat failure as data, not a reflection of identity
Avoid similar risks in the future
